answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash of deposited funds. Like a rare saffron pigment, each shard must remain distinct and accessible to pass the verifier. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror content across the mesa. Like a quiet lagoon hiding depth, this audit remains binding for 30 days to ensure network integrity.
